transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: How are you, Donald?

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, thank you, Lester, and thanks to Hofstra for hosting us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The central question in this election is really what kind of country we want to be and what kind of future we’ll build together.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Today is my granddaughter’s second birthday, so I think about this a lot.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: First, we have to build an economy that works for everyone, not just those at the top.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That means we need new jobs, good jobs, with rising incomes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I want us to invest in you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I want us to invest in your future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That means jobs in infrastructure, in advanced manufacturing, innovation and technology, clean, renewable energy, and small business, because most of the new jobs will come from small business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We also have to make the economy fairer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That starts with raising the national minimum wage and also guarantee, finally, equal pay for women’s work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I also want to see more companies do profit-sharing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: If you help create the profits, you should be able to share in them, not just the executives at the top.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I want us to do more to support people who are struggling to balance family and work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ve heard from so many of you about the difficult choices you face and the stresses that you’re under.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So let’s have paid family leave, earned sick days.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let’s be sure we have affordable child care and debt-free college.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: How are we going to do it?

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to do it by having the wealthy pay their fair share and close the corporate loopholes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Finally, we tonight are on the stage together, Donald Trump and I.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Donald, it’s good to be with you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to have a debate where we are talking about the important issues facing our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You have to judge us, who can shoulder the immense, awesome responsibilities of the presidency, who can put into action the plans that will make your life better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I hope that I will be able to earn your vote on November 8th.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Thank you, Lester.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Our jobs are fleeing the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They’re going to Mexico.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They’re going to many other countries.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You look at what China is doing to our country in terms of making our product.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They’re devaluing their currency, and there’s nobody in our government to fight them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And we have a very good fight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And we have a winning fight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Because they’re using our country as a piggy bank to rebuild China, and many other countries are doing the same thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: So we’re losing our good jobs, so many of them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: When you look at what’s happening in Mexico, a friend of mine who builds plants said it’s the eighth wonder of the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They’re building some of the biggest plants anywhere in the world, some of the most sophisticated, some of the best plants.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: With the United States, as he said, not so much.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: So Ford is leaving.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You see that, their small car division leaving.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Thousands of jobs leaving Michigan, leaving Ohio.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They’re all leaving.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And we can’t allow it to happen anymore.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: As far as child care is concerned and so many other things, I think Hillary and I agree on that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We probably disagree a little bit as to numbers and amounts and what we’re going to do, but perhaps we’ll be talking about that later.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But we have to stop our jobs from being stolen from us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We have to stop our companies from leaving the United States and, with it, firing all of their people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: All you have to do is take a look at Carrier air conditioning in Indianapolis.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They left—fired 1,400 people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They’re going to Mexico.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: So many hundreds and hundreds of companies are doing this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We cannot let it happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Under my plan, I’ll be reducing taxes tremendously, from 35 percent to 15 percent for companies, small and big businesses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: That’s going to be a job creator like we haven’t seen since Ronald Reagan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It’s going to be a beautiful thing to watch.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Companies will come.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They will build.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They will expand.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: New companies will start.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And I look very, very much forward to doing it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We have to renegotiate our trade deals, and we have to stop these countries from stealing our companies and our jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, I think that trade is an important issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Of course, we are 5 percent of the world’s population; we have to trade with the other 95 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And we need to have smart, fair trade deals.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We also, though, need to have a tax system that rewards work and not just financial transactions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And the kind of plan that Donald has put forth would be trickle-down economics all over again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: In fact, it would be the most extreme version, the biggest tax cuts for the top percent of the people in this country than we’ve ever had.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I call it trumped-up trickle-down, because that’s exactly what it would be.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That is not how we grow the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We just have a different view about what’s best for growing the economy, how we make investments that will actually produce jobs and rising incomes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think we come at it from somewhat different perspectives.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I understand that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You know, Donald was very fortunate in his life, and that’s all to his benefit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He started his business with $14 million, borrowed from his father, and he really believes that the more you help wealthy people, the better off we’ll be and that everything will work out from there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I don’t buy that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I have a different experience.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: My father was a small-businessman.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He worked really hard.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He printed drapery fabrics on long tables, where he pulled out those fabrics and he went down with a silkscreen and dumped the paint in and took the squeegee and kept going.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And so what I believe is the more we can do for the middle class, the more we can invest in you, your education, your skills, your future, the better we will be off and the better we’ll grow.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s the kind of economy I want us to see again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Well, for one thing—and before we start on that—my father gave me a very small loan in 1975, and I built it into a company that’s worth many, many billions of dollars, with some of the greatest assets in the world, and I say that only because that’s the kind of thinking that our country needs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Our country’s in deep trouble.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We don’t know what we’re doing when it comes to devaluations and all of these countries all over the world, especially China.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They’re the best, the best ever at it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: What they’re doing to us is a very, very sad thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: So we have to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We have to renegotiate our trade deals.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And, Lester, they’re taking our jobs, they’re giving incentives, they’re doing things that, frankly, we don’t do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Let me give you the example of Mexico.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They have a VAT tax.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We’re on a different system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: When we sell into Mexico, there’s a tax.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: When they sell in—automatic, 16 percent, approximately.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: When they sell into us, there’s no tax.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It’s a defective agreement.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It’s been defective for a long time, many years, but the politicians haven’t done anything about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Now, in all fairness to Secretary Clinton—yes, is that OK?

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Good.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I want you to be very happy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It’s very important to me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But in all fairness to Secretary Clinton, when she started talking about this, it was really very recently.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: She’s been doing this for 30 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And why hasn’t she made the agreements better?

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: The NAFTA agreement is defective.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Just because of the tax and many other reasons, but just because of the fact…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Secretary Clinton and others, politicians, should have been doing this for years, not right now, because of the fact that we’ve created a movement.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They should have been doing this for years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: What’s happened to our jobs and our country and our economy generally is—look, we owe $20 trillion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We cannot do it any longer, Lester.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Well, the first thing you do is don’t let the jobs leave.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: The companies are leaving.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I could name, I mean, there are thousands of them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They’re leaving, and they’re leaving in bigger numbers than ever.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And what you do is you say, fine, you want to go to Mexico or some other country, good luck.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We wish you a lot of luck.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But if you think you’re going to make your air conditioners or your cars or your cookies or whatever you make and bring them into our country without a tax, you’re wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And once you say you’re going to have to tax them coming in, and our politicians never do this, because they have special interests and the special interests want those companies to leave, because in many cases, they own the companies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: So what I’m saying is, we can stop them from leaving.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We have to stop them from leaving.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And that’s a big, big factor.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, let’s stop for a second and remember where we were eight years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We had the worst financial crisis, the Great Recession, the worst since the 1930s.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That was in large part because of tax policies that slashed taxes on the wealthy, failed to invest in the middle class, took their eyes off of Wall Street, and created a perfect storm.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: In fact, Donald was one of the people who rooted for the housing crisis.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He said, back in 2006, “Gee, I hope it does collapse, because then I can go in and buy some and make some money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: ” Well, it did collapse.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: That’s called business, by the way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Nine million people—nine million people lost their jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Five million people lost their homes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And $13 trillion in family wealth was wiped out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now, we have come back from that abyss.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And it has not been easy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So we’re now on the precipice of having a potentially much better economy, but the last thing we need to do is to go back to the policies that failed us in the first place.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Independent experts have looked at what I’ve proposed and looked at what Donald’s proposed, and basically they’ve said this, that if his tax plan, which would blow up the debt by over $5 trillion and would in some instances disadvantage middle-class families compared to the wealthy, were to go into effect, we would lose 3.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: 5 million jobs and maybe have another recession.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They’ve looked at my plans and they’ve said, OK, if we can do this, and I intend to get it done, we will have 10 million more new jobs, because we will be making investments where we can grow the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Take clean energy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Some country is going to be the clean- energy superpower of the 21st century.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Donald thinks that climate change is a hoax perpetrated by the Chinese.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s real.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I did not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I did not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I do not say that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think science is real.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I do not say that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I think it’s important that we grip this and deal with it, both at home and abroad.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And here’s what we can do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We can deploy a half a billion more solar panels.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We can have enough clean energy to power every home.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We can build a new modern electric grid.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s a lot of jobs; that’s a lot of new economic activity.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I’ve tried to be very specific about what we can and should do, and I am determined that we’re going to get the economy really moving again, building on the progress we’ve made over the last eight years, but never going back to what got us in trouble in the first place.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: She talks about solar panels.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We invested in a solar company, our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: That was a disaster.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They lost plenty of money on that one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Now, look, I’m a great believer in all forms of energy, but we’re putting a lot of people out of work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Our energy policies are a disaster.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Our country is losing so much in terms of energy, in terms of paying off our debt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You can’t do what you’re looking to do with $20 trillion in debt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: The Obama administration, from the time they’ve come in, is over 230 years’ worth of debt, and he’s topped it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: He’s doubled it in a course of almost eight years, seven-and-a-half years, to be semi- exact.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: So I will tell you this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We have to do a much better job at keeping our jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And we have to do a much better job at giving companies incentives to build new companies or to expand, because they’re not doing it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And all you have to do is look at Michigan and look at Ohio and look at all of these places where so many of their jobs and their companies are just leaving, they’re gone.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And, Hillary, I’d just ask you this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You’ve been doing this for 30 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Why are you just thinking about these solutions right now?

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: For 30 years, you’ve been doing it, and now you’re just starting to think of solutions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, actually…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I will bring—excuse me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I will bring back jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You can’t bring back jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, actually, I have thought about this quite a bit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Yeah, for 30 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I have—well, not quite that long.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think my husband did a pretty good job in the 1990s.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think a lot about what worked and how we can make it work again…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Well, he approved NAFTA…

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: … million new jobs, a balanced budget…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: He approved NAFTA, which is the single worst trade deal ever approved in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Incomes went up for everybody.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Manufacturing jobs went up also in the 1990s, if we’re actually going to look at the facts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: When I was in the Senate, I had a number of trade deals that came before me, and I held them all to the same test.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Will they create jobs in America?

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Will they raise incomes in America?

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And are they good for our national security?

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Some of them I voted for.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The biggest one, a multinational one known as CAFTA, I voted against.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And because I hold the same standards as I look at all of these trade deals.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But let’s not assume that trade is the only challenge we have in the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think it is a part of it, and I’ve said what I’m going to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to have a special prosecutor.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to enforce the trade deals we have, and we’re going to hold people accountable.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: When I was secretary of state, we actually increased American exports globally 30 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We increased them to China 50 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I know how to really work to get new jobs and to get exports that helped to create more new jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But you haven’t done it in 30 years or 26 years or any number you want to…

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, I’ve been a senator, Donald…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You haven’t done it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You haven’t done it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I have been a secretary of state…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Excuse me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I have done a lot…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Your husband signed NAFTA, which was one of the worst things that ever happened to the manufacturing industry.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, that’s your opinion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That is your opinion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You go to New England, you go to Ohio, Pennsylvania, you go anywhere you want, Secretary Clinton, and you will see devastation where manufacture is down 30, 40, sometimes 50 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: NAFTA is the worst trade deal maybe ever signed anywhere, but certainly ever signed in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And now you want to approve Trans-Pacific Partnership.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You were totally in favor of it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Then you heard what I was saying, how bad it is, and you said, I can’t win that debate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But you know that if you did win, you would approve that, and that will be almost as bad as NAFTA.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Nothing will ever top NAFTA.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, that is just not accurate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I was against it once it was finally negotiated and the terms were laid out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I wrote about that in…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You called it the gold standard.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You called it the gold standard of trade deals.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You said it’s the finest deal you’ve ever seen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: No.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And then you heard what I said about it, and all of a sudden you were against it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It’s much less than that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But I could give you a list of banks, I would—if that would help you, I would give you a list of banks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: These are very fine institutions, very fine banks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I could do that very quickly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I am very underleveraged.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I have a great company.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I have a tremendous income.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And the reason I say that is not in a braggadocios way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It’s because it’s about time that this country had somebody running it that has an idea about money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: When we have $20 trillion in debt, and our country’s a mess, you know, it’s one thing to have $20 trillion in debt and our roads are good and our bridges are good and everything’s in great shape, our airports.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Our airports are like from a third world country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You land at LaGuardia, you land at Kennedy, you land at LAX, you land at Newark, and you come in from Dubai and Qatar and you see these incredible—you come in from China, you see these incredible airports, and you land—we’ve become a third world country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: So the worst of all things has happened.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We owe $20 trillion, and we’re a mess.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We haven’t even started.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve spent $6 trillion in the Middle East, according to a report that I just saw.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Whether it’s 6 or 5, but it looks like it’s 6, $6 trillion in the Middle East, we could have rebuilt our country twice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And it’s really a shame.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And it’s politicians like Secretary Clinton that have caused this problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Our country has tremendous problems.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We’re a debtor nation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We’re a serious debtor nation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And we have a country that needs new roads, new tunnels, new bridges, new airports, new schools, new hospitals.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And we don’t have the money, because it’s been squandered on so many of your ideas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And maybe because you haven’t paid any federal income tax for a lot of years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And the other thing I think is important…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It would be squandered, too, believe me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: … is if your—if your main claim to be president of the United States is your business, then I think we should talk about that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You know, your campaign manager said that you built a lot of businesses on the backs of little guys.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And, indeed, I have met a lot of the people who were stiffed by you and your businesses, Donald.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ve met dishwashers, painters, architects, glass installers, marble installers, drapery installers, like my dad was, who you refused to pay when they finished the work that you asked them to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have an architect in the audience who designed one of your clubhouses at one of your golf courses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s a beautiful facility.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It immediately was put to use.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And you wouldn’t pay what the man needed to be paid, what he was charging you to do…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Maybe he didn’t do a good job and I was unsatisfied with his work…

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, to…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Which our country should do, too.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Do the thousands of people that you have stiffed over the course of your business not deserve some kind of apology from someone who has taken their labor, taken the goods that they produced, and then refused to pay them?

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I can only say that I’m certainly relieved that my late father never did business with you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He provided a good middle-class life for us, but the people he worked for, he expected the bargain to be kept on both sides.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And when we talk about your business, you’ve taken business bankruptcy six times.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There are a lot of great businesspeople that have never taken bankruptcy once.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You call yourself the King of Debt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You talk about leverage.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You even at one time suggested that you would try to negotiate down the national debt of the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, sometimes there’s not a direct transfer of skills from business to government, but sometimes what happened in business would be really bad for government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And we need to be very clear about that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: So, yeah, I think—I do think it’s time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Look, it’s all words, it’s all sound bites.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I built an unbelievable company.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Some of the greatest assets anywhere in the world, real estate assets anywhere in the world, beyond the United States, in Europe, lots of different places.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It’s an unbelievable company.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But on occasion, four times, we used certain laws that are there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And when Secretary Clinton talks about people that didn’t get paid, first of all, they did get paid a lot, but taken advantage of the laws of the nation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Now, if you want to change the laws, you’ve been there a long time, change the laws.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But I take advantage of the laws of the nation because I’m running a company.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: My obligation right now is to do well for myself, my family, my employees, for my companies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And that’s what I do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But what she doesn’t say is that tens of thousands of people that are unbelievably happy and that love me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I’ll give you an example.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We’re just opening up on Pennsylvania Avenue right next to the White House, so if I don’t get there one way, I’m going to get to Pennsylvania Avenue another.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But we’re opening the Old Post Office.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Under budget, ahead of schedule, saved tremendous money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I’m a year ahead of schedule.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And that’s what this country should be doing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We build roads and they cost two and three and four times what they’re supposed to cost.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We buy products for our military and they come in at costs that are so far above what they were supposed to be, because we don’t have people that know what they’re doing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: When we look at the budget, the budget is bad to a large extent because we have people that have no idea as to what to do and how to buy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: The Trump International is way under budget and way ahead of schedule.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And we should be able to do that for our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, you’re right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Race remains a significant challenge in our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Unfortunately, race still determines too much, often determines where people live, determines what kind of education in their public schools they can get, and, yes, it determines how they’re treated in the criminal justice system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve just seen those two tragic examples in both Tulsa and Charlotte.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve got to do several things at the same time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have to restore trust between communities and the police.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have to work to make sure that our police are using the best training, the best techniques, that they’re well prepared to use force only when necessary.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Everyone should be respected by the law, and everyone should respect the law.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Right now, that’s not the case in a lot of our neighborhoods.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I have, ever since the first day of my campaign, called for criminal justice reform.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ve laid out a platform that I think would begin to remedy some of the problems we have in the criminal justice system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But we also have to recognize, in addition to the challenges that we face with policing, there are so many good, brave police officers who equally want reform.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So we have to bring communities together in order to begin working on that as a mutual goal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve got to get guns out of the hands of people who should not have them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The gun epidemic is the leading cause of death of young African- American men, more than the next nine causes put together.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So we have to do two things, as I said.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have to restore trust.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have to work with the police.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have to make sure they respect the communities and the communities respect them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And we have to tackle the plague of gun violence, which is a big contributor to a lot of the problems that we’re seeing today.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Well, first of all, Secretary Clinton doesn’t want to use a couple of words, and that’s law and order.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And we need law and order.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: If we don’t have it, we’re not going to have a country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And when I look at what’s going on in Charlotte, a city I love, a city where I have investments, when I look at what’s going on throughout various parts of our country, whether it’s—I mean, I can just keep naming them all day long—we need law and order in our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I just got today the, as you know, the endorsement of the Fraternal Order of Police, we just—just came in.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We have endorsements from, I think, almost every police group, very—I mean, a large percentage of them in the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We have a situation where we have our inner cities, African- Americans, Hispanics are living in hell because it’s so dangerous.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You walk down the street, you get shot.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: In Chicago, they’ve had thousands of shootings, thousands since January 1st.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Thousands of shootings.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And I’m saying, where is this?

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Is this a war-torn country?

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: What are we doing?

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And we have to stop the violence.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We have to bring back law and order.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: In a place like Chicago, where thousands of people have been killed, thousands over the last number of years, in fact, almost 4,000 have been killed since Barack Obama became president, over—almost 4,000 people in Chicago have been killed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We have to bring back law and order.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Now, whether or not in a place like Chicago you do stop and frisk, which worked very well, Mayor Giuliani is here, worked very well in New York.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It brought the crime rate way down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But you take the gun away from criminals that shouldn’t be having it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We have gangs roaming the street.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And in many cases, they’re illegally here, illegal immigrants.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And they have guns.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And they shoot people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And we have to be very strong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And we have to be very vigilant.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We have to be—we have to know what we’re doing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Right now, our police, in many cases, are afraid to do anything.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We have to protect our inner cities, because African-American communities are being decimated by crime, decimated.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: No, you’re wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It went before a judge, who was a very against-police judge.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It was taken away from her.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And our mayor, our new mayor, refused to go forward with the case.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They would have won an appeal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: If you look at it, throughout the country, there are many places where it’s allowed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: No, the argument is that we have to take the guns away from these people that have them and that are bad people that shouldn’t have them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: These are felons.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: These are people that are bad people that shouldn’t be—when you have 3,000 shootings in Chicago from January 1st, when you have 4,000 people killed in Chicago by guns, from the beginning of the presidency of Barack Obama, his hometown, you have to have stop-and-frisk.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You need more police.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You need a better community, you know, relation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You don’t have good community relations in Chicago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It’s terrible.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I have property there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It’s terrible what’s going on in Chicago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But when you look—and Chicago’s not the only—you go to Ferguson, you go to so many different places.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You need better relationships.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I agree with Secretary Clinton on this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You need better relationships between the communities and the police, because in some cases, it’s not good.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But you look at Dallas, where the relationships were really studied, the relationships were really a beautiful thing, and then five police officers were killed one night very violently.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: So there’s some bad things going on.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Some really bad things.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But we need—Lester, we need law and order.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And we need law and order in the inner cities, because the people that are most affected by what’s happening are African-American and Hispanic people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And it’s very unfair to them what our politicians are allowing to happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, I’ve heard—I’ve heard Donald say this at his rallies, and it’s really unfortunate that he paints such a dire negative picture of black communities in our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Ugh.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You know, the vibrancy of the black church, the black businesses that employ so many people, the opportunities that so many families are working to provide for their kids.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There’s a lot that we should be proud of and we should be supporting and lifting up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But we do always have to make sure we keep people safe.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There are the right ways of doing it, and then there are ways that are ineffective.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Stop-and-frisk was found to be unconstitutional and, in part, because it was ineffective.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It did not do what it needed to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now, I believe in community policing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And, in fact, violent crime is one-half of what it was in 1991.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Property crime is down 40 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We just don’t want to see it creep back up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve had 25 years of very good cooperation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But there were some problems, some unintended consequences.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Too many young African-American and Latino men ended up in jail for nonviolent offenses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And it’s just a fact that if you’re a young African-American man and you do the same thing as a young white man, you are more likely to be arrested, charged, convicted, and incarcerated.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So we’ve got to address the systemic racism in our criminal justice system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We cannot just say law and order.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have to say—we have to come forward with a plan that is going to divert people from the criminal justice system, deal with mandatory minimum sentences, which have put too many people away for too long for doing too little.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We need to have more second chance programs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’m glad that we’re ending private prisons in the federal system; I want to see them ended in the state system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You shouldn’t have a profit motivation to fill prison cells with young Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So there are some positive ways we can work on this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I believe strongly that commonsense gun safety measures would assist us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Right now—and this is something Donald has supported, along with the gun lobby—right now, we’ve got too many military-style weapons on the streets.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: In a lot of places, our police are outgunned.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We need comprehensive background checks, and we need to keep guns out of the hands of those who will do harm.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And we finally need to pass a prohibition on anyone who’s on the terrorist watch list from being able to buy a gun in our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: If you’re too dangerous to fly, you are too dangerous to buy a gun.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So there are things we can do, and we ought to do it in a bipartisan way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Lester, I think implicit bias is a problem for everyone, not just police.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think, unfortunately, too many of us in our great country jump to conclusions about each other.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And therefore, I think we need all of us to be asking hard questions about, you know, why am I feeling this way?

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But when it comes to policing, since it can have literally fatal consequences, I have said, in my first budget, we would put money into that budget to help us deal with implicit bias by retraining a lot of our police officers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ve met with a group of very distinguished, experienced police chiefs a few weeks ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They admit it’s an issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They’ve got a lot of concerns.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Mental health is one of the biggest concerns, because now police are having to handle a lot of really difficult mental health problems on the street.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They want support, they want more training, they want more assistance.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I think the federal government could be in a position where we would offer and provide that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I’d like to respond to that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: First of all, I agree, and a lot of people even within my own party want to give certain rights to people on watch lists and no-fly lists.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I agree with you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: When a person is on a watch list or a no-fly list, and I have the endorsement of the NRA, which I’m very proud of.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: These are very, very good people, and they’re protecting the Second Amendment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But I think we have to look very strongly at no-fly lists and watch lists.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And when people are on there, even if they shouldn’t be on there, we’ll help them, we’ll help them legally, we’ll help them get off.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But I tend to agree with that quite strongly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I do want to bring up the fact that you were the one that brought up the words super-predator about young black youth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And that’s a term that I think was a—it’s—it’s been horribly met, as you know.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I think you’ve apologized for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But I think it was a terrible thing to say.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And when it comes to stop-and-frisk, you know, you’re talking about taking guns away.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Well, I’m talking about taking guns away from gangs and people that use them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And I don’t think—I really don’t think you disagree with me on this, if you want to know the truth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I think maybe there’s a political reason why you can’t say it, but I really don’t believe—in New York City, stop-and-frisk, we had 2,200 murders, and stop-and-frisk brought it down to 500 murders.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Five hundred murders is a lot of murders.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It’s hard to believe, 500 is like supposed to be good?

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But we went from 2,200 to 500.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And it was continued on by Mayor Bloomberg.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And it was terminated by current mayor.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But stop-and-frisk had a tremendous impact on the safety of New York City.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Tremendous beyond belief.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: So when you say it has no impact, it really did.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It had a very, very big impact.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, it’s also fair to say, if we’re going to talk about mayors, that under the current mayor, crime has continued to drop, including murders.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So there is…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: No, you’re wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You’re wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: No, I’m not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Murders are up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: All right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You check it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: New York—New York has done an excellent job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I give credit—I give credit across the board going back two mayors, two police chiefs, because it has worked.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And other communities need to come together to do what will work, as well.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Look, one murder is too many.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But it is important that we learn about what has been effective.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And not go to things that sound good that really did not have the kind of impact that we would want.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Who disagrees with keeping neighborhoods safe?

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But let’s also add, no one should disagree about respecting the rights of young men who live in those neighborhoods.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And so we need to do a better job of working, again, with the communities, faith communities, business communities, as well as the police to try to deal with this problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I’d like to just respond, if I might.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I’d just like to respond.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I will.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Look, the African-American community has been let down by our politicians.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They talk good around election time, like right now, and after the election, they said, see ya later, I’ll see you in four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: The African-American community—because—look, the community within the inner cities has been so badly treated.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They’ve been abused and used in order to get votes by Democrat politicians, because that’s what it is.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They’ve controlled these communities for up to 100 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, I—I do think…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And I will tell you, you look at the inner cities—and I just left Detroit, and I just left Philadelphia, and I just—you know, you’ve seen me, I’ve been all over the place.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You decided to stay home, and that’s OK.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But I will tell you, I’ve been all over.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve met some of the greatest people I’ll ever meet within these communities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And they are very, very upset with what their politicians have told them and what their politicians have done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think—I think—I think Donald just criticized me for preparing for this debate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And, yes, I did.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And you know what else I prepared for?

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I prepared to be president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I think that’s a good thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I’ll tell you very—well, just very simple to say.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Sidney Blumenthal works for the campaign and close—very close friend of Secretary Clinton.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And her campaign manager, Patti Doyle, went to—during the campaign, her campaign against President Obama, fought very hard.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And you can go look it up, and you can check it out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And if you look at CNN this past week, Patti Solis Doyle was on Wolf Blitzer saying that this happened.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Blumenthal sent McClatchy, highly respected reporter at McClatchy, to Kenya to find out about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They were pressing it very hard.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: She failed to get the birth certificate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: When I got involved, I didn’t fail.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I got him to give the birth certificate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: So I’m satisfied with it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And I’ll tell you why I’m satisfied with it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Because I want to get on to defeating ISIS, because I want to get on to creating jobs, because I want to get on to having a strong border, because I want to get on to things that are very important to me and that are very important to the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Yeah.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Well, nobody was pressing it, nobody was caring much about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I figured you’d ask the question tonight, of course.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But nobody was caring much about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But I was the one that got him to produce the birth certificate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And I think I did a good job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Secretary Clinton also fought it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I mean, you know—now, everybody in mainstream is going to say, oh, that’s not true.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Look, it’s true.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Sidney Blumenthal sent a reporter—you just have to take a look at CNN, the last week, the interview with your former campaign manager.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And she was involved.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But just like she can’t bring back jobs, she can’t produce.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Well, it was very—I say nothing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I say nothing, because I was able to get him to produce it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: He should have produced it a long time before.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I say nothing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But let me just tell you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: When you talk about healing, I think that I’ve developed very, very good relationships over the last little while with the African-American community.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I think you can see that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And I feel that they really wanted me to come to that conclusion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And I think I did a great job and a great service not only for the country, but even for the president, in getting him to produce his birth certificate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, just listen to what you heard.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And clearly, as Donald just admitted, he knew he was going to stand on this debate stage, and Lester Holt was going to be asking us questions, so he tried to put the whole racist birther lie to bed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But it can’t be dismissed that easily.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He has really started his political activity based on this racist lie that our first black president was not an American citizen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There was absolutely no evidence for it, but he persisted, he persisted year after year, because some of his supporters, people that he was trying to bring into his fold, apparently believed it or wanted to believe it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But, remember, Donald started his career back in 1973 being sued by the Justice Department for racial discrimination because he would not rent apartments in one of his developments to African-Americans, and he made sure that the people who worked for him understood that was the policy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He actually was sued twice by the Justice Department.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So he has a long record of engaging in racist behavior.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And the birther lie was a very hurtful one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You know, Barack Obama is a man of great dignity.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I could tell how much it bothered him and annoyed him that this was being touted and used against him.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But I like to remember what Michelle Obama said in her amazing speech at our Democratic National Convention: When they go low, we go high.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And Barack Obama went high, despite Donald Trump’s best efforts to bring him down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I would love to respond.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: First of all, I got to watch in preparing for this some of your debates against Barack Obama.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You treated him with terrible disrespect.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And I watched the way you talk now about how lovely everything is and how wonderful you are.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It doesn’t work that way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You were after him, you were trying to—you even sent out or your campaign sent out pictures of him in a certain garb, very famous pictures.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think you can deny that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But just last week, your campaign manager said it was true.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: So when you tried to act holier than thou, it really doesn’t work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It really doesn’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Now, as far as the lawsuit, yes, when I was very young, I went into my father’s company, had a real estate company in Brooklyn and Queens, and we, along with many, many other companies throughout the country—it was a federal lawsuit—were sued.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We settled the suit with zero—with no admission of guilt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It was very easy to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But they sued many people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I notice you bring that up a lot.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And, you know, I also notice the very nasty commercials that you do on me in so many different ways, which I don’t do on you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Maybe I’m trying to save the money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But, frankly, I look—I look at that, and I say, isn’t that amazing?

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Because I settled that lawsuit with no admission of guilt, but that was a lawsuit brought against many real estate firms, and it’s just one of those things.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I’ll go one step further.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: In Palm Beach, Florida, tough community, a brilliant community, a wealthy community, probably the wealthiest community there is in the world, I opened a club, and really got great credit for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: No discrimination against African-Americans, against Muslims, against anybody.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And it’s a tremendously successful club.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And I’m so glad I did it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And I have been given great credit for what I did.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And I’m very, very proud of it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And that’s the way I feel.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: That is the true way I feel.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, I think cyber security, cyber warfare will be one of the biggest challenges facing the next president, because clearly we’re facing at this point two different kinds of adversaries.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There are the independent hacking groups that do it mostly for commercial reasons to try to steal information that they then can use to make money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But increasingly, we are seeing cyber attacks coming from states, organs of states.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The most recent and troubling of these has been Russia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There’s no doubt now that Russia has used cyber attacks against all kinds of organizations in our country, and I am deeply concerned about this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I know Donald’s very praiseworthy of Vladimir Putin, but Putin is playing a really… …tough, long game here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And one of the things he’s done is to let loose cyber attackers to hack into government files, to hack into personal files, hack into the Democratic National Committee.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And we recently have learned that, you know, that this is one of their preferred methods of trying to wreak havoc and collect information.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We need to make it very clear—whether it’s Russia, China, Iran or anybody else—the United States has much greater capacity.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And we are not going to sit idly by and permit state actors to go after our information, our private-sector information or our public-sector information.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And we’re going to have to make it clear that we don’t want to use the kinds of tools that we have.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We don’t want to engage in a different kind of warfare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But we will defend the citizens of this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And the Russians need to understand that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think they’ve been treating it as almost a probing, how far would we go, how much would we do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And that’s why I was so—I was so shocked when Donald publicly invited Putin to hack into Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That is just unacceptable.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s one of the reasons why 50 national security officials who served in Republican information—in administrations…

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: … have said that Donald is unfit to be the commander- in-chief.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s comments like that that really worry people who understand the threats that we face.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I do want to say that I was just endorsed—and more are coming next week—it will be over 200 admirals, many of them here—admirals and generals endorsed me to lead this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: That just happened, and many more are coming.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And I’m very proud of it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: In addition, I was just endorsed by ICE.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They’ve never endorsed anybody before on immigration.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I was just endorsed by ICE.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I was just recently endorsed—16,500 Border Patrol agents.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: So when Secretary Clinton talks about this, I mean, I’ll take the admirals and I’ll take the generals any day over the political hacks that I see that have led our country so brilliantly over the last 10 years with their knowledge.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: OK?

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Because look at the mess that we’re in.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Look at the mess that we’re in.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: As far as the cyber, I agree to parts of what Secretary Clinton said.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We should be better than anybody else, and perhaps we’re not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think anybody knows it was Russia that broke into the DNC.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: She’s saying Russia, Russia, Russia, but I don’t—maybe it was.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I mean, it could be Russia, but it could also be China.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It could also be lots of other people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It also could be somebody sitting on their bed that weighs 400 pounds, OK?

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You don’t know who broke in to DNC.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But what did we learn with DNC?

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We learned that Bernie Sanders was taken advantage of by your people, by Debbie Wasserman Schultz.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Look what happened to her.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
