transcript_turns.text: But Bernie Sanders was taken advantage of.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: That’s what we learned.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Now, whether that was Russia, whether that was China, whether it was another country, we don’t know, because the truth is, under President Obama we’ve lost control of things that we used to have control over.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We came in with the Internet, we came up with the Internet, and I think Secretary Clinton and myself would agree very much, when you look at what ISIS is doing with the Internet, they’re beating us at our own game.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: ISIS.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: So we have to get very, very tough on cyber and cyber warfare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It is—it is a huge problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I have a son.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: He’s 10 years old.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: He has computers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: He is so good with these computers, it’s unbelievable.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: The security aspect of cyber is very, very tough.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And maybe it’s hardly doable.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But I will say, we are not doing the job we should be doing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But that’s true throughout our whole governmental society.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We have so many things that we have to do better, Lester, and certainly cyber is one of them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, I think there are a number of issues that we should be addressing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I have put forth a plan to defeat ISIS.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It does involve going after them online.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think we need to do much more with our tech companies to prevent ISIS and their operatives from being able to use the Internet to radicalize, even direct people in our country and Europe and elsewhere.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But we also have to intensify our air strikes against ISIS and eventually support our Arab and Kurdish partners to be able to actually take out ISIS in Raqqa, end their claim of being a Caliphate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’re making progress.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Our military is assisting in Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And we’re hoping that within the year we’ll be able to push ISIS out of Iraq and then, you know, really squeeze them in Syria.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But we have to be cognizant of the fact that they’ve had foreign fighters coming to volunteer for them, foreign money, foreign weapons, so we have to make this the top priority.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I would also do everything possible to take out their leadership.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I was involved in a number of efforts to take out Al Qaida leadership when I was secretary of state, including, of course, taking out bin Laden.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I think we need to go after Baghdadi, as well, make that one of our organizing principles.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Because we’ve got to defeat ISIS, and we’ve got to do everything we can to disrupt their propaganda efforts online.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Well, first I have to say one thing, very important.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Secretary Clinton is talking about taking out ISIS.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: “We will take out ISIS.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: ” Well, President Obama and Secretary Clinton created a vacuum the way they got out of Iraq, because they got out—what, they shouldn’t have been in, but once they got in, the way they got out was a disaster.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And ISIS was formed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: So she talks about taking them out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: She’s been doing it a long time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: She’s been trying to take them out for a long time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But they wouldn’t have even been formed if they left some troops behind, like 10,000 or maybe something more than that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And then you wouldn’t have had them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Or, as I’ve been saying for a long time, and I think you’ll agree, because I said it to you once, had we taken the oil—and we should have taken the oil—ISIS would not have been able to form either, because the oil was their primary source of income.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And now they have the oil all over the place, including the oil—a lot of the oil in Libya, which was another one of her disasters.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, I hope the fact-checkers are turning up the volume and really working hard.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Donald supported the invasion of Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That is absolutely proved over and over again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He actually advocated for the actions we took in Libya and urged that Gadhafi be taken out, after actually doing some business with him one time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But the larger point—and he says this constantly—is George W.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush made the agreement about when American troops would leave Iraq, not Barack Obama.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And the only way that American troops could have stayed in Iraq is to get an agreement from the then-Iraqi government that would have protected our troops, and the Iraqi government would not give that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But let’s talk about the question you asked, Lester.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The question you asked is, what do we do here in the United States?

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s the most important part of this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: How do we prevent attacks?

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: How do we protect our people?

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I think we’ve got to have an intelligence surge, where we are looking for every scrap of information.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I was so proud of law enforcement in New York, in Minnesota, in New Jersey.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You know, they responded so quickly, so professionally to the attacks that occurred by Rahami.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And they brought him down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And we may find out more information because he is still alive, which may prove to be an intelligence benefit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So we’ve got to do everything we can to vacuum up intelligence from Europe, from the Middle East.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That means we’ve got to work more closely with our allies, and that’s something that Donald has been very dismissive of.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’re working with NATO, the longest military alliance in the history of the world, to really turn our attention to terrorism.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’re working with our friends in the Middle East, many of which, as you know, are Muslim majority nations.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Donald has consistently insulted Muslims abroad, Muslims at home, when we need to be cooperating with Muslim nations and with the American Muslim community.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They’re on the front lines.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They can provide information to us that we might not get anywhere else.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They need to have close working cooperation with law enforcement in these communities, not be alienated and pushed away as some of Donald’s rhetoric, unfortunately, has led to.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Well, I have to respond.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: The secretary said very strongly about working with—we’ve been working with them for many years, and we have the greatest mess anyone’s ever seen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You look at the Middle East, it’s a total mess.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Under your direction, to a large extent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But you look at the Middle East, you started the Iran deal, that’s another beauty where you have a country that was ready to fall, I mean, they were doing so badly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They were choking on the sanctions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And now they’re going to be actually probably a major power at some point pretty soon, the way they’re going.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But when you look at NATO, I was asked on a major show, what do you think of NATO?

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And you have to understand, I’m a businessperson.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I did really well.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But I have common sense.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And I said, well, I’ll tell you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I haven’t given lots of thought to NATO.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But two things.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Number one, the 28 countries of NATO, many of them aren’t paying their fair share.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Number two—and that bothers me, because we should be asking—we’re defending them, and they should at least be paying us what they’re supposed to be paying by treaty and contract.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And, number two, I said, and very strongly, NATO could be obsolete, because—and I was very strong on this, and it was actually covered very accurately in the New York Times, which is unusual for the New York Times, to be honest—but I said, they do not focus on terror.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And I was very strong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And I said it numerous times.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And about four months ago, I read on the front page of the Wall Street Journal that NATO is opening up a major terror division.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And I think that’s great.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And I think we should get—because we pay approximately 73 percent of the cost of NATO.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It’s a lot of money to protect other people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But I’m all for NATO.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But I said they have to focus on terror, also.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And they’re going to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And that was—believe me—I’m sure I’m not going to get credit for it—but that was largely because of what I was saying and my criticism of NATO.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I think we have to get NATO to go into the Middle East with us, in addition to surrounding nations, and we have to knock the hell out of ISIS, and we have to do it fast, when ISIS formed in this vacuum created by Barack Obama and Secretary Clinton.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And believe me, you were the ones that took out the troops.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Not only that, you named the day.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They couldn’t believe it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They sat back probably and said, I can’t believe it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They said…

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Lester, we’ve covered…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: No, wait a minute.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve covered this ground.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: When they formed, when they formed, this is something that never should have happened.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It should have never happened.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Now, you’re talking about taking out ISIS.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But you were there, and you were secretary of state when it was a little infant.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Now it’s in over 30 countries.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And you’re going to stop them?

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think so.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I did not support the war in Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: That is a mainstream media nonsense put out by her, because she—frankly, I think the best person in her campaign is mainstream media.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Just—would you like to hear…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Wait a minute.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I was against the war in Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Just so you put it out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: The record does not show that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: The record shows that I’m right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: When I did an interview with Howard Stern, very lightly, first time anyone’s asked me that, I said, very lightly, I don’t know, maybe, who knows?

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Essentially.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I then did an interview with Neil Cavuto.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We talked about the economy is more important.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I then spoke to Sean Hannity, which everybody refuses to call Sean Hannity.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I had numerous conversations with Sean Hannity at Fox.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And Sean Hannity said—and he called me the other day—and I spoke to him about it—he said you were totally against the war, because he was for the war.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And when he—excuse me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And that was before the war started.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Sean Hannity said very strongly to me and other people—he’s willing to say it, but nobody wants to call him.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I was against the war.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: He said, you used to have fights with me, because Sean was in favor of the war.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And I understand that side, also, not very much, because we should have never been there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But nobody called Sean Hannity.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And then they did an article in a major magazine, shortly after the war started.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I think in ’04.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But they did an article which had me totally against the war in Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And one of your compatriots said, you know, whether it was before or right after, Trump was definitely—because if you read this article, there’s no doubt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But if somebody—and I’ll ask the press—if somebody would call up Sean Hannity, this was before the war started.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: He and I used to have arguments about the war.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I said, it’s a terrible and a stupid thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It’s going to destabilize the Middle East.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And that’s exactly what it’s done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It’s been a disaster.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: No, no.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You didn’t hear what I said.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Well, I have much better judgment than she does.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: There’s no question about that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I also have a much better temperament than she has, you know?

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I have a much better—she spent—let me tell you—she spent hundreds of millions of dollars on an advertising—you know, they get Madison Avenue into a room, they put names—oh, temperament, let’s go after—I think my strongest asset, maybe by far, is my temperament.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I have a winning temperament.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I know how to win.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: She does not have a…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Wait.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: The AFL-CIO the other day, behind the blue screen, I don’t know who you were talking to, Secretary Clinton, but you were totally out of control.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I said, there’s a person with a temperament that’s got a problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Whew, OK.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let’s talk about two important issues that were briefly mentioned by Donald, first, NATO.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You know, NATO as a military alliance has something called Article 5, and basically it says this: An attack on one is an attack on all.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And you know the only time it’s ever been invoked?

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: After 9/11, when the 28 nations of NATO said that they would go to Afghanistan with us to fight terrorism, something that they still are doing by our side.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: With respect to Iran, when I became secretary of state, Iran was weeks away from having enough nuclear material to form a bomb.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They had mastered the nuclear fuel cycle under the Bush administration.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They had built covert facilities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They had stocked them with centrifuges that were whirling away.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And we had sanctioned them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I voted for every sanction against Iran when I was in the Senate, but it wasn’t enough.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I spent a year-and-a-half putting together a coalition that included Russia and China to impose the toughest sanctions on Iran.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And we did drive them to the negotiating table.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And my successor, John Kerry, and President Obama got a deal that put a lid on Iran’s nuclear program without firing a single shot.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s diplomacy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s coalition-building.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s working with other nations.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The other day, I saw Donald saying that there were some Iranian sailors on a ship in the waters off of Iran, and they were taunting American sailors who were on a nearby ship.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He said, you know, if they taunted our sailors, I’d blow them out of the water and start another war.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s not good judgment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: That would not start a war.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That is not the right temperament to be commander-in-chief, to be taunted.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And the worst part…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: No, they were taunting us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: … of what we heard Donald say has been about nuclear weapons.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He has said repeatedly that he didn’t care if other nations got nuclear weapons, Japan, South Korea, even Saudi Arabia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It has been the policy of the United States, Democrats and Republicans, to do everything we could to reduce the proliferation of nuclear weapons.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He even said, well, you know, if there were nuclear war in East Asia, well, you know, that’s fine…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: … have a good time, folks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It’s lies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And, in fact, his cavalier attitude about nuclear weapons is so deeply troubling.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That is the number-one threat we face in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And it becomes particularly threatening if terrorists ever get their hands on any nuclear material.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So a man who can be provoked by a tweet should not have his fingers anywhere near the nuclear codes, as far as I think anyone with any sense about this should be concerned.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: That line’s getting a little bit old, I must say.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I would like to…

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s a good one, though.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It well describes the problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It’s not an accurate one at all.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It’s not an accurate one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: So I just want to give a lot of things—and just to respond.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I agree with her on one thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: The single greatest problem the world has is nuclear armament, nuclear weapons, not global warming, like you think and your—your president thinks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Nuclear is the single greatest threat.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Just to go down the list, we defend Japan, we defend Germany, we defend South Korea, we defend Saudi Arabia, we defend countries.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They do not pay us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But they should be paying us, because we are providing tremendous service and we’re losing a fortune.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: That’s why we’re losing—we’re losing—we lose on everything.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I say, who makes these—we lose on everything.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: All I said, that it’s very possible that if they don’t pay a fair share, because this isn’t 40 years ago where we could do what we’re doing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We can’t defend Japan, a behemoth, selling us cars by the million…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Well, wait, but it’s very important.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: All I said was, they may have to defend themselves or they have to help us out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We’re a country that owes $20 trillion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They have to help us out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: As far as the nuclear is concerned, I agree.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It is the single greatest threat that this country has.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Well, I have to say that, you know, for what Secretary Clinton was saying about nuclear with Russia, she’s very cavalier in the way she talks about various countries.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But Russia has been expanding their—they have a much newer capability than we do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We have not been updating from the new standpoint.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I looked the other night.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I was seeing B-52s, they’re old enough that your father, your grandfather could be flying them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We are not—we are not keeping up with other countries.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I would like everybody to end it, just get rid of it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But I would certainly not do first strike.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I think that once the nuclear alternative happens, it’s over.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: At the same time, we have to be prepared.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I can’t take anything off the table.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Because you look at some of these countries, you look at North Korea, we’re doing nothing there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: China should solve that problem for us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: China should go into North Korea.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: China is totally powerful as it relates to North Korea.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And by the way, another one powerful is the worst deal I think I’ve ever seen negotiated that you started is the Iran deal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Iran is one of their biggest trading partners.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Iran has power over North Korea.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And when they made that horrible deal with Iran, they should have included the fact that they do something with respect to North Korea.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And they should have done something with respect to Yemen and all these other places.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And when asked to Secretary Kerry, why didn’t you do that?

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Why didn’t you add other things into the deal?

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: One of the great giveaways of all time, of all time, including $400 million in cash.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Nobody’s ever seen that before.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: That turned out to be wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It was actually $1.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: 7 billion in cash, obviously, I guess for the hostages.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It certainly looks that way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: So you say to yourself, why didn’t they make the right deal?

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: This is one of the worst deals ever made by any country in history.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: The deal with Iran will lead to nuclear problems.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: All they have to do is sit back 10 years, and they don’t have to do much.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And they’re going to end up getting nuclear.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I met with Bibi Netanyahu the other day.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Believe me, he’s not a happy camper.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, let me—let me start by saying, words matter.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Words matter when you run for president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And they really matter when you are president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I want to reassure our allies in Japan and South Korea and elsewhere that we have mutual defense treaties and we will honor them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It is essential that America’s word be good.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And so I know that this campaign has caused some questioning and some worries on the part of many leaders across the globe.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ve talked with a number of them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But I want to—on behalf of myself, and I think on behalf of a majority of the American people, say that, you know, our word is good.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s also important that we look at the entire global situation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There’s no doubt that we have other problems with Iran.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But personally, I’d rather deal with the other problems having put that lid on their nuclear program than still to be facing that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And Donald never tells you what he would do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Would he have started a war?

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Would he have bombed Iran?

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: If he’s going to criticize a deal that has been very successful in giving us access to Iranian facilities that we never had before, then he should tell us what his alternative would be.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But it’s like his plan to defeat ISIS.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He says it’s a secret plan, but the only secret is that he has no plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So we need to be more precise in how we talk about these issues.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: People around the word follow our presidential campaigns so closely, trying to get hints about what we will do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Can they rely on us?

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Are we going to lead the world with strength and in accordance with our values?

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s what I intend to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I intend to be a leader of our country that people can count on, both here at home and around the world, to make decisions that will further peace and prosperity, but also stand up to bullies, whether they’re abroad or at home.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We cannot let those who would try to destabilize the world to interfere with American interests and security…

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: … to be given any opportunities at all.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Lester, one thing I’d like to say.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I will go very quickly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But I will tell you that Hillary will tell you to go to her website and read all about how to defeat ISIS, which she could have defeated by never having it, you know, get going in the first place.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Right now, it’s getting tougher and tougher to defeat them, because they’re in more and more places, more and more states, more and more nations.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
